draft.title: Consumer law and marketing
card: The Australian Consumer Law (ACL) is a national law that applies to businesses across Australia. It protects consumers and sets rules for how businesses market and sell goods and services.
Misleading claims
A business must not make false or misleading statements about a product, its price or its benefits. A claim can mislead through what it leaves out, or through the way it is worded.
Consumer guarantees

Goods and services must meet basic standards. For example, goods must be of acceptable quality and must match their description. If they fail, the consumer can ask for a remedy such as a repair, replacement or refund.
Unfair practices
Businesses must not use unfair tactics such as pressuring buyers, advertising a bargain they do not intend to supply, or using unfair contract terms.
draft.remember: The ACL makes marketers tell the truth, deliver what they promise and treat buyers fairly.

a.q: An online shop advertises a jacket as 'waterproof', but it leaks in light rain. Which part of the ACL has the shop most clearly breached?
opts: The rule against false or misleading claims
The rule against unfair contract terms
The rule against pressuring buyers to purchase
The rule requiring a repair, replacement or refund
a.why: The shop made a claim about the product that is not true, so it is a false or misleading claim. The remedy rule is tempting, but it applies after a product fails. The marketing breach here is the untrue statement.
a.clue: Look at what the advertisement said about the jacket.

b.q: Priya buys a blender from a store in Parramatta. It stops working after two weeks of normal use. The store refuses help because the sale was not on special. Which statement is correct under the ACL?
opts: Priya can seek a remedy, as the blender is not acceptable quality
Priya cannot, as only goods on special are covered by guarantees
Priya cannot, as the store made no claim about the blender
Priya cannot, as two weeks of use ends the store's duty
b.why: Consumer guarantees apply to goods whether or not they are on special. A blender that fails in two weeks of normal use is unlikely to be of acceptable quality, so Priya can seek a repair, replacement or refund. The store does not need to have made a claim for the guarantee to apply.
b.clue: Consumer guarantees do not depend on the price paid or on what the seller said.

proposal.title: Consumer law and marketing
card: The Australian Consumer Law (ACL) is a national law that applies to businesses across Australia. It protects consumers and sets rules for how businesses market and sell goods and services.
Misleading claims
A business must not make false or misleading statements about a product, its price or its benefits. A claim can mislead through what it leaves out, or through the way it is worded.
Consumer guarantees

Goods must meet basic standards, such as being of acceptable quality and matching their description, even if bought on sale or sold with no promises. If they fail, the consumer can ask for a remedy such as a repair, replacement or refund.
Unfair practices
Businesses must not use unfair tactics such as harassing or coercing buyers, advertising a bargain they do not intend to supply, or using unfair contract terms. Ordinary sales persuasion is allowed.
proposal.remember: The ACL makes marketers tell the truth, deliver what they promise and treat buyers fairly.

a.q: An online shop advertises a jacket as 'waterproof', but it leaks in light rain. Which part of the ACL has the shop most clearly breached?
opts: The rule against false or misleading claims
The rule against unfair contract terms
The rule against harassing or coercing buyers
The rule requiring a repair, replacement or refund
a.why: The shop made a claim about the product that is not true, so it is a false or misleading claim. The remedy rule is tempting, but it applies after a product fails. The marketing breach here is the untrue statement.
a.clue: Look at what the advertisement said about the jacket.

b.q: Priya buys a blender at a sale price from a store in Parramatta. It stops working after two weeks of normal use. The store says sale items are not covered. Which statement is correct under the ACL?
opts: Priya can seek a remedy, as the guarantees still apply
Priya can seek a remedy only if the store chooses to help
Priya has no remedy, as sale items are not covered
Priya has no remedy, as the store made no claim about it
b.why: Consumer guarantees apply even when goods are bought on sale. A blender that fails after two weeks of normal use is unlikely to be of acceptable quality, so Priya can ask for a repair, replacement or refund. The guarantee is a right under the law, not a favour the store can choose to give, and it does not depend on the store making a claim.
b.clue: Does a sale price change the basic standards goods must meet?
